Every Janmashtami, grown men stack themselves nine people high... to smash one clay pot. Why? Blame a five-year-old. Gokul. Krishna loves butter. Like, really loves butter.
So he steals it. From every house in the village. The women of Gokul are done. Their plan? Hang the butter pots high, where tiny hands can't reach.
Problem solved, they think. Krishna looks up. Looks at his friends. And whistles. One kneels down. One climbs on his shoulders. Then another.
Wait, why are the climbers called Govindas today? Because that's his name. Little Krishna climbs to the very top, reaches out... and crack! Butter rains down on the whole gang.
Mother Yashoda walks in. Hands on her hips. Krishna, covered in butter, gives her the sweetest smile. And she can't stay angry.
Today, from Mumbai to Mathura, they still do it. Because the women built a wall... and Krishna built a team. Comment Govinda if you've seen one.
